main_text.head: Quæstio XXV.
An furor Principis, an populi magis exitialis sit?
main_text.p: ATrocior est noster quam Jovis ignis: Alpes hic ferit & turrium apices, securæ valles humilesque casæ; Ille dum furit, ventorum forte flatibus irritatus, tecta, templa, sylvas, segetes, ima pariter ac summa, nullo corripit discrimine: Sic dum Principis aliquantisper simultate pressa intumuit ira, crepat illa cominùs, & stragem edit in Satrapas: tutum est eminùs Terræ Filiis spectaculum; At si vulgi turbulenta rabies, Legis excusserit capistrum, contumaci ungulâ Ruit omnia latè: Fas, nefas, sacra, profana susque deque O

page.notes: The opening letter A is a large woodcut initial, joined to the word "Trocior" as "ATrocior". The left margin strip belongs to the facing page and is not transcribed. The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page; the word "O" and "deque" are set as printed, with "O" centred and "deque" right-aligned. Marks "ungulâ" carries a circumflex as printed.
